value.reason: In routes/orderHistory.ts:16-17, the email is turned into a lookup key by replacing every vowel with '*' (`email.replace(/[aeiou]/gi, '*')`). Orders are then fetched by that key alone (`ordersCollection.find({ email: updatedEmail })`). This change loses information, so different addresses end up with the same key. For example, '«EMAIL»', '«EMAIL»' and '«EMAIL»' all become 'b*«UPI»*m'. Someone who signs up with an address that collides with a victim's address gets the victim's order history from the public route GET /rest/order-history (server.ts:663). The order records include Contact data written by datacreator.ts:798. Even if the email comes from the logged-in session rather than the request, the result is the same. The safe example has a collision check (it rejects a request when another account masks to the same value) and a second ownership check on each record. Neither appears in this Evidence. The pattern matches the positive example: the record key can be chosen or forged by a user and is the only ownership check, which is the broken object-level authorization described in CWE-639 and OWASP API1:2023. It is also a failure of the access-control safeguards required by DPDP Rule 6(1)(b).
